chunks: A group informed me, from Abu Muhammad Harun, from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Himam, who said:

And on the ring of Abu Ja'far al-Samman (may Allah be pleased with him) was engraved: 'La ilaha illallah al-Malik al-Haqq al-Mubin.' I asked him about it, and he said: Abu Muhammad (meaning the Master of the Army, Imam Hasan al-Askari, peace be upon him) narrated from his forefathers (peace be upon them) that they said: Lady Fatima (peace be upon her) had a ring with a cornelian stone. When her death approached, she handed it to Hasan (peace be upon him). When his death approached, he handed it to Husayn (peace be upon him). Husayn (peace be upon him) said: I desired to engrave something on it, and I saw in a dream the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon our Prophet and his family and him. I said to him: O Spirit of Allah, what should I engrave on this ring of mine? He said: Engrave on it: 'La ilaha illallah al-Malik al-Haqq al-Mubin.' For it is the first [verse] of the Torah and the last [verse] of the Gospel.

key_terms.المسيح عيسى بن مريم: The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary
key_terms.صاحب العسكر: The Master of the Army (Imam Hasan al-Askari)

ai.seo_question: What inscription did Imam Husayn engrave on his ring based on the dream of Jesus?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the spiritual continuity of the Ahl al-Bayt through the transmission of Lady Fatima’s agate ring to Imam Husayn, who received divine instruction from Prophet Jesus (Isa) in a vision. The inscription 'La ilaha illallah al-Malik al-Haqq al-Mubin' is significant in Shia tradition as a unifying creed linking the Torah and the Gospel, emphasizing the esoteric truth (Haqq) and manifest clarity (Mubin) of divine sovereignty. This narrative underscores the inter-prophetic connection within the Shia understanding of the Imamate and the preservation of sacred knowledge.
